key_insight: A stable Galerkin reduced-order model combined with an extended Kalman filter can accurately estimate the full Rayleigh-Bénard convection state from sparse measurements, even using velocity data alone.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical framework for real-time flow monitoring, sensor reduction, and state reconstruction in CFD systems where full-field measurements are unavailable.
method: Build a stable ROM from controllability modes of the linearised Boussinesq equations.
Use the ROM as the EKF prediction model and DNS-generated synthetic data for assimilation.
Apply the Kalman gain to rank sensors and iteratively remove the least informative ones.
evidence_signal: Across periodic, quasiperiodic, and chaotic regimes, the method tracked energetic modes well and achieved time-averaged reconstruction errors below 14% for velocity and 9% for temperature.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the ROM and the measurement model, so transfer to noisier experiments or different parameter regimes may require re-tuning and validation.
paper_title: State estimation of Rayleigh-Bénard convection with reduced-order models
